title: Service-Gradient Fallback Controller: burst isolation and progressive throughput guarantees
creator: Leah Martinez
description: Problem statement: Dedicated fleets must simultaneously provide per-customer throughput guarantees while absorbing bursts from noisy tenants and preserving SLOs for tiered customers. Current controls (static token buckets + coarse shedder) either overthrottle during transient spikes or fail to isolate bursts, causing SLO violations for other tenants. This ticket proposes a Service-Gradient Fallback Controller (SGFC) to provide predictable headroom allocation, burst isolation, and staged fallback policies tied to autoscaler signals.
background: We currently use queue-depth thresholds, a global shedder, and per-tenant rate caps. Several incidents in Q4 and Q1 demonstrated: (1) sudden headroom collapse when autoscaler lagged behind traffic spikes, (2) noisy tenants consuming transient slots and causing p95/p99 latency regressions for premium customers, (3) opaque fallback behavior when model variant downgrade kicks in. The SGFC is intended to be the central orchestrator that converts capacity signals (autoscaler states, KV cache hit rates, GPU utilization) into admission decisions with clear priority semantics.
proposal: Design a controller that assigns each active tenant a dynamic 'service gradient' (weight + reservoir) computed from SLA tier, committed throughput, recent error/latency history, and predictive autoscaler forecasts. Admission proceeds in three stages: (A) fast admission path using preallocated reservoir tokens for low-latency requests, (B) queued low-priority window with sub-second soft queueing and latency compensation, and (C) progressive shedder that degrades non-critical requests by routing to cheaper model variants or bounded rejection with informative error payloads. The controller exposes a control API to the serving runtime to: (1) request token allocation, (2) subscribe to reservoir drain events, and (3) request fallback decisions. It also emits detailed observability events for billing and SLO attribution.
design_notes: Key components: (1) Gradient calculator service (stateless stream processor) that ingests rate/capacity metrics and assigns gradients every 100ms; (2) Reservoir allocator (per-fleet persistent store) that holds burst credits and enforces tenant isolation; (3) Soft-queue runtime shim that preserves KV cache locality by prioritizing requests with recent cache hits; (4) Fallback manager that resolves routing to model variants and backoff back to primary variant. We prefer a conservative rollout: feature flag default-off, canary on a single low-traffic region, and rollout to one fleet size at a time.
acceptance_criteria: SGFC computes and exposes per-tenant service gradients every 100-250ms in production canary
Reservoir allocation prevents a single tenant from consuming more than 15% of headroom during sustained bursts (verified by synthetic tests)
P99 latency for P0 customers on canary fleet does not regress more than 5% under controlled burst scenarios
Autoscaler-inferred headroom changes trigger deterministic reallocation within 300ms
Fallback manager successfully routes to preconfigured model variants and emits structured events for every fallback decision
End-to-end integration test coverage for token request, queue admission, and fallback flows with mocked autoscaler signals
rollout_plan: Canary: enable on dedicated-fleet-us-west-2-small for 72h with synthetic burst traffic
Monitor telemetry: per-tenant headroom, reservoir utilization, p95/p99 latency, error-rate, fallback-rate
Iterate thresholds and reservoir refill policy during canary based on metrics and QA signoff
Gradual ramp: enable additional fleets by traffic class (dev -> internal -> premium -> all) over 4 weeks
Full rollout conditioned on no SLO regressions and runbook verification
tasks: Implement Gradient Calculator stream job (Kafka -> Flink/Beam prototype)
Add Reservoir persistent store API and CLI for manual adjustments
Integrate runtime shim to query token allocation synchronously (low-latency path)
Implement soft-queue prioritization logic in serving runtime with KV cache affinity
Build Fallback Manager that maps tenants to fallback model variants and exposes API
Create end-to-end integration tests and load tests (k6/jmeter) for burst scenarios
Add observability dashboard in Console: reservoir heatmaps, per-tenant fallback traces, headroom drift
Author runbook for triage steps when SGFC triggers mass fallback or reservoir exhaustion
Security review for control-plane RPCs and reservoir access patterns
metrics: P95/P99 latency for each SLA tier
Fallback rate (routes to downgraded model) per 10-minute window
Autoscaler lag: time between forecasted demand inflection and actual scaling event
Number of rejected requests attributed to SGFC vs underlying runtime
open_questions: Reservoir sizing heuristic: should it be proportional to committed throughput or historical burstiness?
How to reconcile multi-tenant KV cache locality when requests are rerouted to fallback models?
What is the SLO contract surface we expose to customers when fallback is used (informational vs billed)?
Do we maintain per-tenant persistent reservoirs across restarts or treat them as ephemeral per-epoch?
Can the autoscaler provide tighter forecasts (short-horizon) to reduce reactive shedding?
